subject: gk
question: Which of the following denotes the ideals that the state should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles Of State Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India.

• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.

• They aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.

• The DPSPs are included in Part IV of the Constitution of India, from Articles 36 to 51.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Preamble**

• The Preamble to the Constitution of India is a brief introductory statement that sets out the guiding purpose and principles of the document.

• It indicates the source from which the Constitution derives its authority and states the objectives which the Constitution seeks to establish and promote.

• The Preamble declares India to be a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic.

• It assures its citizens of justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity among them.

• **Fundamental Rights**

• Fundamental Rights are a group of rights that are recognized by the Constitution of India as being essential for the existence and development of individuals.

• These rights are enforceable by the courts, subject to specific restrictions.

• They include rights such as the right to equality, freedom, against exploitation, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.

• They are included in Part III of the Constitution, from Articles 12 to 35.

• **Fundamental Duties**

• Fundamental Duties are a set of moral obligations that all citizens are expected to follow to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.

• These duties are not enforceable by law but serve as a constant reminder to citizens of their responsibilities towards the country.

• They are included in Part IV-A of the Constitution, under Article 51A.

• There are 11 Fundamental Duties, which were added by the 42nd and 86th Constitutional Amendments.
